narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Thread"**

A task is a conversation with the agent doing the work. The app sits on a soft sage ground, and every piece of content is a white rounded sheet laid on it: header, brief, details, runs, the agent's messages. The run transcript and the human conversation read like a messaging thread: the agent speaks from the left in white bubbles, you answer from the right in green bubbles, and the machinery in between (tool calls, thoughts, log lines, phase changes, git notes) collapses into small pill chips and centred notes so it never outshouts what was said.

Density is moderate and calm: 14px body text, 20px gaps between sheets, soft hairlines instead of rules. Colour is scarce and semantic. Deep green is the agent and the primary action; warm orange is reserved for the one thing a human must act on. Everything else is sage-tinted neutral. The system explicitly refuses the category default: a dark zinc sidebar dashboard of dense tables and status badges.

Light is the default theme; dark (`.dark` on `<html>`) is a full parallel palette on a near-black green ground, not an inversion.
keyCharacteristics: Sage ground under white rounded sheets; sheets separate by tone, with only a hairline in the border tone.
Deep green for the agent and primary actions; orange only for "needs a human".
Pills everywhere a thing is a status, a phase or an action; 16px bubbles for speech; 14px sheets for containers.
Figtree for all UI text, DM Mono only for code, paths, keys and numbers.
Lucide line icons, never glyphs or emoji.
No raster imagery: the app ships no images; avatars are initials on colour tiles.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Green belongs to the agent and to "do it"; orange belongs to "a human must decide". No third accent. Task status maps accordingly: In progress is primary green (with a 3px green halo on its dot), In review is human orange, Done is success green; Backlog, Todo and Cancelled stay neutral.

rules.name: The Scarce Orange Rule
rules.body: Orange appears only where a human is waited on. If nothing on the screen needs a person, no orange is visible.

rules.name: The Mono Is Machine Text Rule
rules.body: DM Mono is for code, paths, keys and numbers only. Never for headings, labels or decoration.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels and chips are sentence case at 0.75rem semibold. No uppercase tracked micro-labels above headings.

rules.name: The Tone Before Shadow Rule
rules.body: A sheet on the ground separates by colour and a hairline; it does not get a shadow at rest. Shadow is for speech and for things floating over other content.

dos: Do put content on white sheets (14px radius, 1px hairline) over the sage ground; keep the run thread itself on the ground.
Do use agent green for the agent, the primary action and the live state, and nothing decorative.
Do reserve orange for "needs a human": In review, Needs review, and future human-decision states.
Do make statuses, phases, chips and buttons full pills.
Do give speech 16px bubbles with an 8px tail corner on the speaker's side.
Do set code, paths, task keys, SHAs, counts, costs and timers in DM Mono with tabular numbers.
Do use Lucide line icons at 16px (12-14px inside small pills).
Do honour `prefers-reduced-motion`: the global rule collapses animations and hides the live ping.
donts: Don't fall into the category default: a dark zinc sidebar dashboard of dense tables and status badges.
Don't introduce a third accent or use orange for decoration, branding or "you" chrome.
Don't draw dark or high-contrast borders around sheets; the hairline tone is the only border colour.
Don't fill destructive buttons with solid red; use the 10% tint.
Don't set UI labels or headings in DM Mono, and don't add uppercase tracked eyebrow labels above headings.
Don't use raw Tailwind palette colours or hard-coded hex in components; every colour comes from a token in `web/src/styles.css`.
Don't give sheets a shadow at rest.
